questions.text: What year of study is Kamila Seitkali?
questions.hint: "I am a second-year student at WKU."

questions.text: How many languages can Kamila speak?
questions.hint: "I can speak three languages: Kazakh, Russian, and English."

questions.text: Kamila can play the guitar.
questions.hint: "Unfortunately, I cannot play the piano or the guitar."

questions.text: How many traditional Kazakh songs can Kamila play on the dombra?
questions.hint: "I can play about twenty traditional Kazakh songs."

questions.text: Everybody calls Amir "The Tech ___".
questions.hint: "Everybody in our group calls him 'The Tech Wizard!'"

questions.text: What can Amir NOT do?
questions.hint: "He cannot cook anything except instant noodles."

questions.text: Rustam can kick the ball with both feet.
questions.hint: "He can kick the ball with both his right foot and his left foot."

questions.text: What skill is Kamila currently learning?
questions.hint: "I am learning to drive a car — but I cannot drive yet!"

questions.text: What talent does Kamila perform at the talent show?
questions.hint: "I can play the dombra — I can play about twenty traditional Kazakh songs."

questions.text: Kamila says she can sing very well.
questions.hint: "I can't sing very well. I'm much better at playing than singing."

questions.text: How long does it take Amir to solve a Rubik's cube?
questions.hint: "I can solve it in under two minutes!"

questions.text: Zhibek can do a ___ on stage.
questions.hint: "I can do a backflip on stage."

questions.text: Rustam can juggle and sing at the same time.
questions.hint: "I can't sing or dance, but I can make a football do anything!"

questions.text: How long can Rustam balance the ball on his head?
questions.hint: "I can balance the ball on my head for thirty seconds."

questions.text: Choose the correct form: She ___ perform three Kazakh dances.
questions.hint: Ability → can. CAN never takes -s.

questions.text: I ___ drive yet — I'm learning every Saturday.
questions.hint: Negative present ability → can't.

questions.text: Which sentence is correct?
questions.hint: CAN + bare infinitive. No -s, no "to".

questions.text: "Can she dances?" is correct English.
questions.hint: After Can → base form: Can she dance?

questions.text: COULD is used to describe ability in...
questions.hint: COULD = past of CAN → past ability.

questions.text: She ___ speak English two years ago — she started learning at university.
questions.hint: "Two years ago" = past + negative → couldn't.

questions.text: Kamila ___ play 20 songs now, but she ___ only play 3 when she started.
questions.hint: Now = can; When she started (past) = could.

questions.text: "He couldn't swam as a child" — what is wrong?
questions.hint: After couldn't → base verb only: couldn't swim (not "swam").

questions.text: What does "ability" mean?
opts: The skill or power to do something
questions.correct: The skill or power to do something
questions.hint: Ability = the skill or power to do something.

questions.text: My biggest ___ is cooking — I cannot even make soup!
questions.hint: Weakness = something you are not good at.

questions.text: What does "dedicated" / "dedication" mean?
opts: Hard work and effort for something you care about
questions.correct: Hard work and effort for something you care about
questions.hint: Dedication = hard work and effort put into something you care about.

questions.text: "Practise" means to do something once to check if it works.
questions.hint: Practise = to do something REGULARLY to improve your skill.

questions.text: What is an "audience"?
opts: The group of people watching a performance
questions.correct: The group of people watching a performance
questions.hint: Audience = the group of people watching a performance.

questions.text: She is very ___ about traditional Kazakh music — she trains every day.
questions.hint: Passionate = having a very strong interest or enthusiasm.

questions.text: What does "confident" mean?
questions.hint: Confident = feeling sure about your abilities.

questions.text: To "achieve" something means to...
opts: successfully reach a goal you worked for
try something for the first time
questions.correct: successfully reach a goal you worked for
questions.hint: Achieve = to successfully do or get something you worked for.
